He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Bucknell Bison men's basketball|Bucknell Bison]] and the [[Penn State Nittany Lions basketball|Penn State Nittany Lions]].{{cite web|title=Andrew Funk - Bucknell Athletics|url=https://bucknellbison.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/andrew-funk/7605|website=BucknellBison.com|access-date=September 1, 2023}}{{cite web|title=Andrew Funk - Penn State Athletics|url=https://gopsusports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/andrew-funk/12858|website=GoPSUSports.com|access-date=September 1, 2023}} ==High school career== Funk played at [[Archbishop Wood Catholic High School|Archbishop Wood High School]]. As a junior, he scored in double figures eleven times and was named Sixth Man of the Year by the [[Philadelphia Inquirer]] while helping the Vikings go 28–3 and win their first Philadelphia Catholic League championship, as well as the Class 5A PIAA state championship and the District 12 title. As a senior, Funk became a team captain and was chosen as the Philadelphia Catholic League Player of the Year, additionally being selected first-team All-PCL and second-team All-Southeast Pennsylvania. ==College career== Funk played his first four [[college basketball]] seasons for [[Bucknell Bison men's basketball|Bucknell]] and his final one at [[Penn State Nittany Lions basketball|Penn State]], finishing his career having totaled 1,693 points (11.5 ppg), 457 rebounds, 302 3-pointers and 237 assists. In his graduate season with the Nittany Lions, he averaged 12.5 points per game, had 25 games with double-digit scoring marks and posted eight games with 20-points, also having a career-high with 44.4 percent shooting from the field and 41.2% from the 3-point range. For his performance, Funk was named honorable mention All-Big Ten and was also elected to the Academic All-District team.{{cite web|title=Bucknell’s Andrew Funk Signs Summer League Deal with Nuggets|url=https://www.wkok.com/bucknells-andrew-funk-signs-summer-league-deal-with-denver-nuggets/|website=WKOK.com|date=June 23, 2023|access-date=September 1, 2023}} During Funk's first and only season at Penn State, the team compiled an overall record of 23–14 and reached the NCAA Tournament for the first time since 2011. Funk scored a team-high 27 points in Penn State's 76-59 first round victory over [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M]], the Nittany Lions' first NCAA Tournament victory since 2001.{{cite web|title=Penn State vs. Texas A&M Box Score (Men), March 16, 2023|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/boxscores/2023-03-16-21-texas-am.html|website=Sports-Reference.com|access-date=February 28, 2024}} ==Professional career== ===Grand Rapids Gold (2023–2024)=== After going undrafted in the [[2023 NBA draft]], Funk joined the [[Denver Nuggets]] for the [[2023 NBA Summer League]]. On July 18, 2023, Funk signed with the Nuggets,{{cite web|title=NUGGETS SIGN ARMAAN FRANKLIN AND ANDREW FUNK TO TRAINING CAMP CONTRACTS|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-armaan-franklin-and-andrew-funk-to-training-camp-contracts|website=NBA.com|date=July 18, 2023|access-date=September 1, 2023}} but was waived on October 13.{{cite web|title=DENVER NUGGETS SIGN BRIMAH, TONEY AND PICKETT|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/denver-nuggets-sign-brimah-toney-and-pickett|website=NBA.com|date=October 13, 2023|access-date=October 15, 2023}} On October 30, he joined the [[Grand Rapids Gold]].{{cite tweet|author=Grand Rapids Gold|title=Time to get to work ⏰ It’s #GOldTime|number=1719081989876199493|user=NBAGrandRapids|date=October 30, 2023|access-date=January 30, 2024}} In 24 games with the Gold, Funk averaged 13.4 points, 3.4 rebounds and 3.5 assists per game.{{cite web|title=Bulls sign Andrew Funk to two-way contract|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-andrew-funk-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=February 25, 2024|access-date=February 25, 2024}} ===Chicago / Windy City Bulls (2024)=== On February 25, 2024, Funk signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Chicago Bulls]]. Funk made his [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] debut in a 126–111 loss to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] on March 14, logging one minute.{{cite web|title=Clippers 126-111 Bulls (Mar 14, 2024) Final Score|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/game/_/gameId/401585584/clippers-bulls|website=ESPN.com|access-date=March 17, 2024}} On July 24, he was waived by the Bulls after playing in five games without scoring. {{cite tweet|author=Chicago Bulls|title=Transaction: We have waived Andrew Funk. Thank you and best of luck, Andrew.|number=1816214067058528675|user=chicagobulls|date=July 24, 2024|access-date=July 25, 2024}} ===Return to Grand Rapids (2024–2025)=== On October 8, 2024, Funk signed with the [[Denver Nuggets]],{{cite web|title=NUGGETS SIGN WILL RICHARDSON, ANDREW FUNK, AND CHARLES BEDIAKO|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-will-richardson-andrew-funk-and-charles-bediako|website=NBA.com|date=October 8, 2024|access-date=October 8, 2024}} but was waived on October 16.{{cite web|first=Dana|last=Gauruder|title=Spurs’ McDaniels Among Wednesday’s Cuts|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/10/spurs-mcdaniels-among-wednesdays-cuts.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 16, 2024|access-date=October 19, 2024}} On October 28, he rejoined the [[Grand Rapids Gold]].{{cite web|title=Gold Finalize 2024-25 Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/gold-finalize-2024-25-training-camp-roster/n-6160538|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 28, 2024|access-date=November 3, 2024}} ===Antwerp Giants (2025–2026)=== On July 25, 2025, he signed with [[Antwerp Giants]] of the [[BNXT League]].{{Cite web|url=https://antwerpgiants.be/andrew-funk-naar-windrose-giants-antwerp/|title=Andrew Funk naar Windrose Giants Antwerp|date=July 25, 2025|website=antwerpgiants.be|publisher=|language=be|access-date=August 1, 2025}} ==Personal life== He is the son of Theresa and Albert Funk and has four brothers. He graduated with a bachelor's degree in business administration from [[Bucknell University|Bucknell]] and earned a master's degree in management and organizational leadership at [[Pennsylvania State
